page: Amazon Web Services m8i.large is a general-purpose instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor running at 3.9 GHz. The instance provides 2 vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 8.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 7 GHz, yielding 4.0 GB of memory per core. Local storage is not bundled, and the baseline network bandwidth is 1 Gbps.

The underlying Intel Xeon processor includes a 480 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1D cache. It supports advanced instruction sets such as Intel Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX, AVX512F, AVX512_VNNI, AVX_VNNI, AVX512_BF16) and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX_TILE, AMX_INT8). Cryptographic acceleration is supported via AES, VAES, and SHA_NI flags.

Benchmark data reveals strong single-core performance, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2169.0 and strong single-threaded compression metrics, including 34.22 GB/sec for gzip and 14.28 GB/sec for bzip3. However, multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics are generally weak. The stress-ng multi-core CPU performance is rated poor at 2158.78, and the Geekbench multi-core score is weak at 2735.0. Memory bandwidth for large uncached blocks is poor, measuring 22.61 GB/sec for read and 17.99 GB/sec for write operations.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the m8i.large offers a modern DDR5 memory subsystem and dedicated CPU allocation for entry-level general-purpose workloads, though its low core count limits parallel processing efficiency. It is suitable for single-threaded tasks, basic web serving, text processing, and lightweight development environments, but is constrained for database operations, heavy multi-threaded compilation, or large-scale LLM inference.
